protocol: Aircraft altitude at the event was 600 ft on a carrier approach. The cabin was overpressurized before abrupt decompression. The peak cabin overpressure was not quantified.
outcome_window: Substernal discomfort and cough five minutes after landing. Reevaluation at 20 hours after the event led to hyperbaric treatment. No recurrence was reported during a 14-day grounding period.
note: Two selected clinician-diagnosed Type II DCS episodes. The affected exposure population and incident dates were not given.

protocol: Aircraft at 30,000 ft. Cabin pressure altitude fluctuated from 11,000 to 18,000 ft and then to 9,000 ft. The figure provides a trace illustration and no machine-readable trace.
outcome_window: Initial in-flight chest symptoms. First flight-surgeon evaluation 90 minutes after the event. Later neurological deficits off oxygen prompted confirmation of the clinical DCS diagnosis. Return to flying after 14 days of observation.
note: Two selected clinician-diagnosed Type II DCS episodes. The affected exposure population and incident dates were not given.
